title: The Game of the Year Race Is Wide Open — Here's Who's Leading
summary:
The 13th Game Awards are set for December 10, and the race for Game of the Year is heating up. According to Polygon's analysis, Resident Evil Requiem is currently in pole position. The survival-horror sequel combines the fan appeal of the remakes with the freshness of a new entry. It has a Metacritic score in the high 80s, which is very good — but maybe just a little soft for a true Game of the Year contender. Still, nothing else released this year combines critical acclaim with the perfect Game Awards genre profile so effectively.

Close behind is Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, a tactics RPG from Nintendo. Critics love that it unites strong storytelling with refined combat on an epic canvas. It has an 89 on Metacritic. But there's a catch: the Game Awards jury always nominates Fire Emblem games in the Sim/Strategy category, which never overlaps with Game of the Year. If it gets nominated, it would be the first strategy game ever to break into GOTY consideration.

Then there's 007 First Light, IO Interactive's James Bond game. It earned an 87 Metascore. This kind of slick, cinematic action-adventure usually goes down well with the jury. However, licensed games very rarely get nominated for Game of the Year. Its competition in the action-adventure field has fizzled, notably Marvel's Wolverine, which is out of the running after a poor critical reception.

Control Resonant, a sequel from Remedy, is also in the mix. It has an 84 on Metacritic, higher than the original Control's 82, but the sentiment seems cooler. As a sequel, it may have lost the element of surprise.

With so many potential spoilers flaming out, this year's race is unpredictable. We'll find out who wins on December 10.
why_it_matters: Award shows like this do more than hand out trophies: they shape which genres publishers fund, which games get marketing budgets the following year, and how a jury's category rules can quietly decide who is even eligible to compete. Watching which games break through — or get blocked by a category — shows how much power sits with a small group of judges and with the review scores they lean on.

background_read: The Game Awards (an annual ceremony for video games, created by host Geoff Keighley and held every December since 2014) is not a simple public vote: winners are mostly chosen by a jury of games journalists, with the public making up a smaller share. That structure is why genre categories matter so much — a game that never reaches the Game of the Year list can still dominate its own slot. Metacritic (a site that averages critics' review scores into a single number out of 100) is used industry-wide as shorthand for quality, so 'high 80s' means most critics liked a game a lot, though not universally.

Resident Evil (Capcom's survival-horror series, which began in 1996 and has been remade and rebooted many times) is one of gaming's best-known franchises, so its sequel arrives with both nostalgia and novelty. Fire Emblem (Nintendo's tactics series, launched in 1990, in which players move characters around a grid like chess pieces) has a devoted following but has tended to be filed by awards juries under strategy. IO Interactive (the Danish studio behind the Hitman assassination games) is making 007 First Light, a James Bond game — the Bond franchise has long been controlled by the Broccoli family's Eon Productions and is now partly owned by Amazon MGM. Licensed games, from movie tie-ins to superhero adaptations, have a long history of being rushed out to hit a release date, which is one reason juries treat them cautiously.

perspectives.perspective: Positive — a strong year for the frontrunners
perspectives.description: Resident Evil Requiem arrives with both familiar appeal and something new, and its high-80s Metacritic score reflects broad critical approval, so the jury's favourite is also a genuinely well-reviewed game. If Fire Emblem were nominated it would be a milestone, proving a strategy game can reach the industry's biggest stage.

perspectives.perspective: Negative / critical — the rules may matter more than the games
perspectives.description: 007 First Light has an 87 Metascore but is described as unlikely to be nominated largely because it is a licensed game, and Fire Emblem risks being locked out by its category rather than its quality. That suggests the awards reward genre profile and precedent as much as how good a game actually is, which frustrates developers working outside the favoured categories.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral / analytical — awards have always had blind spots
perspectives.description: Game awards have historically been kind to cinematic action-adventures and less kind to strategy, sports or licensed titles, and juries drawn from the press tend to share similar tastes. Category systems exist to spread recognition, but they can also create ceilings that no single game can break on merit alone.

perspectives.perspective: Forward-looking — what the December result will tell us
perspectives.description: Watch whether a 'soft' high-80s score is enough to carry Resident Evil Requiem to the top, whether Fire Emblem finally cracks the GOTY list, and whether the jury ever revisits how it sorts genres. If it does not, the same structural limits will shape next year's race too.
